summary.brief: Chef Billy Parisi prepares a red‑wine ribeye steak, cooks sea bass in a white‑wine sauce, and makes a fruit sangria.
summary.detailed: The video opens with a title card and a close‑up of red wine being poured into a white bowl. The chef boils equal parts water and sugar to make a simple syrup, then chills it. He chops garlic, shallots, and rosemary, and whiskes them with balsamic vinegar, sugar, grainy mustard, olive oil, the chilled syrup, and Cabernet Sauvignon to create a red‑wine ribeye marinade, which he uses to submerge the steak and refrigerates. While the steak marinates, he prepares a fruit sangria by tossing chopped oranges, berries, and pineapple into a bowl, coating them with the simple syrup, adding cranberry‑raspberry juice, a splash of Zinfandel, and ice, then chilling the mixture. He then turns to a white‑wine sauce: he chops fresh dill, leeks, and lemon, sautés the leeks and garlic in hot olive oil, deglazes with white wine, adds lemon juice, capers, and cold butter, and seasons with salt, pepper, and dill. In a very hot sauté pan he cooks a sea bass fillet in olive oil for three to four minutes per side, then finishes it with the white‑wine sauce. After the marinades have set, he removes the ribeye, seasons it with salt and pepper, and grills it on a hot grill (450‑550 °F) for four to six minutes per side until medium‑rare. Finally, he plates the steak and fish, presents the sangria, shows the completed multi‑course meal, and ends with closing credits and promotional graphics.

summary.brief: Chef Billy Parisi prepares a wine‑marinated steak, a white‑wine fish sauce, and a red‑wine sangria, then plates the dishes with a glass of wine.
summary.detailed: The segment opens with a close‑up of red wine being poured into a white bowl as the chef introduces the lesson. He makes a simple syrup of equal parts water and sugar, then whisks together garlic, shallots, balsamic vinegar, mustard, sugar, rosemary, olive oil and Cabernet Sauvignon to create a wine‑marinade, which he coats on a ribeye steak and sets in the refrigerator. While the steak marinates, he chops a variety of fruit—strawberries, blackberries, blueberries, orange, lemon and pineapple—adds the simple syrup and more red wine to make sangria. summary.brief: Chef Billy Parisi demonstrates a wine‑marinated ribeye, a fruit‑based sangria, and a white‑wine sauce for seared sea bass.
summary.detailed: The segment opens with a close‑up of red wine being poured into a bowl while the chef greets the viewer. He boils equal parts water and sugar to make a simple syrup, then chills it. Using the syrup as a base, he chops garlic and shallots, whiskes them with balsamic vinegar, sugar, grainy mustard, rosemary, olive oil and Cabernet Sauvignon to create a wine‑marinade, into which he submerges a ribeye and places the bag in the refrigerator. He then coats chopped oranges, berries and other fruit with the remaining syrup, adds cranberry‑raspberry juice and a red Zinfandel, and chills the mixture to make sangria. After the steak has marinated, he removes it, seasons it with salt and pepper, and grills it on a very hot grill for a few minutes per side to reach medium‑rare. While the steak cooks, he heats a pan, adds olive oil and a sea bass fillet, caramelizes shallots and garlic, deglazes with white wine, squeezes in lemon juice, adds capers, then finishes the sauce by whisking in cold butter, salt, pepper and fresh dill. The segment ends with the plated steak, the sea‑bass in its lemon‑caper‑dill white‑wine sauce, and the chilled sangria displayed together.

summary.brief: Chef Billy Parisi marinates a ribeye, grills it, prepares a wine‑infused fruit salad, and cooks a lemon‑caper white‑wine sauce for fish with a side of sautéed potatoes and olives.
summary.detailed: He first chops garlic, shallots, rosemary, thyme and other aromatics, then whiskes them together with balsamic vinegar, grainy mustard, olive oil and Cabernet Sauvignon in a bowl, places the ribeye steak in a zip‑lock bag, seals it and refrigerates to marinate. While the steak rests, he tosses assorted fruit in a large white bowl, adds red wine and stirs. After the marination, he seasons the steak with salt and pepper and grills it on a hot grill to medium‑rare. At the same time he sautés a sea bass fillet, caramelizes shallots and garlic, deglazes with lemon juice, capers and white wine, and finishes the sauce with cold butter and fresh dill. He also cooks a side of diced potatoes, olives, lemon juice, wine and butter in a skillet, stirring until tender. Finally he plates the grilled steak, the fish with lemon‑caper white‑wine sauce, and the wine‑infused fruit salad.

summary_sent_to_llm.title: How to cook with wine
summary_sent_to_llm.description: Uncork your bottles and head to the kitchen! Chef Billy Parisi shows us various ways to cook with wine.
summary_sent_to_llm.root_summary: The video opens with a title card and a close‑up of red wine being poured into a white bowl. The chef boils equal parts water and sugar to make a simple syrup, then chills it. He chops garlic, shallots, and rosemary, and whiskes them with balsamic vinegar, sugar, grainy mustard, olive oil, the chilled syrup, and Cabernet Sauvignon to create a red‑wine ribeye marinade, which he uses to submerge the steak and refrigerates. While the steak marinates, he prepares a fruit sangria by tossing chopped oranges, berries, and pineapple into a bowl, coating them with the simple syrup, adding cranberry‑raspberry juice, a splash of Zinfandel, and ice, then chilling the mixture. He then turns to a white‑wine sauce: he chops fresh dill, leeks, and lemon, sautés the leeks and garlic in hot olive oil, deglazes with white wine, adds lemon juice, capers, and cold butter, and seasons with salt, pepper, and dill. In a very hot sauté pan he cooks a sea bass fillet in olive oil for three to four minutes per side, then finishes it with the white‑wine sauce. After the marinades have set, he removes the ribeye, seasons it with salt and pepper, and grills it on a hot grill (450‑550 °F) for four to six minutes per side until medium‑rare. Finally, he plates the steak and fish, presents the sangria, shows the completed multi‑course meal, and ends with closing credits and promotional graphics.
